None. The main papers in Brazil are Folha and Estadão. Folha has a lot of liberal bloggers, but their printed newspaper and their main columns are mostly what one would call "center". They constantly receive criticism from both the left and the right. Last year they published a big article saying their goal is to be as unbiased as possible. Of course there's no such thing. Estadão on the other hand has editorials openly admitting their bias - in the previous elections they openly admitted supporting one of the candidates (the PSDB ones). Globo is the most watched television channel and also has a news website, I would put them next to Folha though they don't have political bloggers. Record and Band are the other television "big guys" (Record is owned by Edir Macedo, a congressman and a priest, I'm not sure where to put Band). There are numerous large newspapers (as Brazil is a large country), but none as large as the aforementioned ones. If you just want to stay informed about Brazil in general without much depth, I'd say go with G1, Globo's news website. It's also the most popular source on the Brazilian subreddit. If you want more depth then get as many sources as you can and also go with blogs and social media. Big media doesn't cover a lot of things that go on here.
